item.title: Up 53 spots! Vaishnavi Sharma makes giant leap in ICC ODI rankings after stunning spells against Zimbabwe
item.description: NEW DELHI: India's 3-0 clean sweep against Zimbabwe in the three-match ODI series has brought several players into the spotlight in the latest ICC Women's ODI Player Rankings, with young spinner Vaishnavi Sharma making the biggest jump after an impressive performance in the series finale. The 20-year-old left-arm spinner climbed an impressive 53 places to reach 94th in the ODI bowling rankings after claiming nine wickets across the second and third matches of the series. It was a remarkable rise for Vaishnavi, who has made an immediate impact in just her first three appearances in the format. After picking up four wickets in the second ODI, Vaishnavi delivered a match-winning performance in the series finale, returning figures of 5/39. Her maiden five-wicket haul in ODIs earned her the Player of the Match award as India completed a comprehensive series sweep in the ICC Women's Championship. Sayali Satghare, Kranti Gaud also rise Vaishnavi was not the only Indian bowler to benefit from the series against Zimbabwe. Sayali Satghare climbed 18 places to 85th in the latest bowling rankings following an impressive outing in the third ODI. The right-arm pacer returned figures of 2/11 from six overs, including 30 dot balls, underlining her effectiveness with the new ball. Kranti Gaud also made progress, moving up one place to 24th after claiming two wickets in Vadodara. Zimbabwe's Nomvelo Sibanda gained two places to reach 60th in the bowling rankings. She made an early impact in the final ODI, dismissing Yastika Bhatia off the first ball of India's innings. Pratika Rawal, Shafali Verma make batting gains There were positive developments for Indian batters as well, with Pratika Rawal continuing her consistent run in the series. The opener climbed three places to 18th after registering her third consecutive half-century against Zimbabwe. Shafali Verma also moved up eight places to joint 65th following her attacking 51-run knock in the series finale. Zimbabwe's batters made progress in the latest update too. Opener Modester Mupachikwa climbed three places to 36th after scoring 37 in the third ODI, while captain Josephine Nkomo gained two spots to reach 49th.

item.title: Un punto más para el Barça en la Youth League (3-3)
item.description: Un punto más para el Barça en la Youth League (3-3) El conjunto azulgrana consigue sumar un punto ante el Aston Villa para escalar posiciones en la clasificación de la UEFA Youth League. Tras un partido lleno de intensidad e intentos, han conseguido igualar el marcador gracias a un gol de Iu Martínez en los últimos instantes del encuentro. Los de Pol Planas tienen dos jornadas más por delante para conseguir su objetivo, ante el Sabah y el Manchester City . El Barça ante el Aston Villa en la Youth League / Sergio Sorolla / @foto.monjo Llegan los refuerzos El Barça salía con todo ante un partido importante con la necesidad de sumar los tres puntos . El técnico apostó por un once inicial de gala para reencontrarse con la victoria en Europa tras el empate ante el PSG . El Barça empezó manteniendo el balón con buenas asociaciones y amplia creatividad para atacar los espacios. Los azulgranas se encontraron con un planteamiento conocido, un rival con falta de ideas sin intención de apretar. Ebrima Tunkara no tardó mucho en demostrar porque habían contado con él para este encuentro. El futbolista azulgrana remató de cabeza con suerte para aprovechar el rechace y abrir el marcador (1-0). El Aston Villa despertó tarde. El conjunto inglés apretaba con tanta fuerza en el tramo final de la primer mitad que pudo lograr igualar el marcador con dos saques de esquina (2-2). Los adversarios recortaron la distancia para dirigirse al descanso un poco más aliviados. Sin embargo, una perspectiva muy diferente a los azulgranas que se marchaban encajando dos goles en cuestión de diez minutos. Cuesta arriba Giro de 180 grados. item.title: Falcons Cut Drake Jackson And Jared Ivey Ahead Of Week 9
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Atlanta Falcons made a quick roster shakeup on Monday afternoon. The team released outside linebacker Jared Ivey and defensive end Drake Jackson just as Week 9 gets ready to start. This move comes right after a rough 16-0 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. The team needs fresh legs to handle the Cincinnati Bengals next Sunday. Per the Atlanta Falcons official report, both players are gone from the 53-man roster effective immediately. Ivey played 17 snaps on Sunday but did not record a single stat. He had been on the roster since the team claimed him off waivers in late August. According to the Atlanta Falcons, he appeared in seven games this season with one sack and two tackles for a loss. He started his career with the Seattle Seahawks and was part of their Super Bowl win in 2025. That title makes his release even more surprising for fans who liked his energy. The team let him go despite his recent playing time and past success. Why the defense needs a spark Drake Jackson played 20 snaps over two games before he got cut. He joined the roster on October 24 after spending last year with the Washington Commanders. Per Heavy.com , he was inactive for the game against Tampa Bay on Sunday. His time in Atlanta was short and unproductive. Although he was selected in the second round from USC, staying healthy has proven difficult for him. Injuries and poor play have hurt his career since he was drafted by the 49ers in 2022. The Falcons are clearly looking for someone else to fill the pass-rush role. The timing of this move points to a specific plan. According to The Falcoholic , James Pearce Jr. is eligible to return from suspension this week. Yasir Abdullah can also come back from injured reserve. These two players offer the speed and run defense the team needs against Joe Burrow. The Falcons likely need the roster spots for these returns. It makes sense to clear the bench for players who have already proven they can play in this system. The Falcons will try to bring Ivey and Jackson back on the practice squad. Heavy.com notes that Ivey is a Super Bowl champion who might land there quickly. Jackson has the pedigree to get another shot too. The team wants to keep them close in case they need depth later. This is a common move for the NFL when teams need to make room for returning stars. It keeps the talent in the building without using a 53-man spot. The defense must fix its run issues before Sunday. The team allowed 16 points and no offense against the Buccaneers. A better pass rush is the only way to stop the Bengals offense.

item.title: Iraola urges Liverpool to 'kill' Fenerbahce's hostile atmosphere
item.description: Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola (BERK OZKAN) Andoni Iraola has urged Liverpool to stop Fenerbahce in Wednesday's Champions League clash by killing the hostile atmosphere generated by their raucous fans. Iraola is expecting a deafening atmosphere at the Sukru Saracoglu stadium in Istanbul, but the Liverpool boss is confident his side can cope with the unwelcoming environment. The Spaniard believes Liverpool must cut off the connection between Fenerbahce's players and their passionate fans by taking the sting out of the game. "Tomorrow, it's not going to be easy. It's always difficult to come to Turkey and play and we have to be very ready," Iraola said on Tuesday. "They have experienced players who know how to play in this competition. We have to try to kill the confidence and momentum they can have with the supporters. "Champions League away days are difficult and we know this, especially in this stadium and atmosphere. We have to be mentally very ready. "We want to continue how we have done in the Champions League. It is a good chance to get to 12 points and then finish in the top eight." Stopping Fenerbahce's momentum in such a febrile atmosphere might be easier said than done for Liverpool. In Sunday's 1-0 defeat against Premier League champions Arsenal, Liverpool failed to register a shot on target in a home league game for the first time since records began in 2003. That lack of cutting edge has been an issue at times for Liverpool this season as they adapt to Iraola's preferred style of play. But their 100 per cent Champions League record this season has seen them score six against LASK, four against Villarreal and two against Atletico Madrid, compared to 11 in nine Premier League matches. Asked if he had learnt from Liverpool's impotence against Arsenal, Iraola added: "It is difficult when you lose but honestly I am happy with a lot of things from the other day. "I liked a lot of things but we still need to improve, especially attacking the box. "A lot of times we were there with the numbers but not making the proper runs and waiting for second balls. "We put Arsenal under pressure and they defended well but I liked a lot of things." Fifth-placed Liverpool are already nine points behind leaders Arsenal in the title race. It is hardly the start Iraola would have been hoping for in his first season since arriving from Bournemouth to replace the sacked Arne Slot. "I think we have had better results in the Champions League and Carabao Cup but it's very early in the season to establish comparisons," Iraola said. Liverpool will be without Dutch midfielder Ryan Gravenberch, who was left at home after reporting discomfort with a heel problem during the warm-up on Sunday. smg/iwd

item.description: There are a lot of new faces that the #17/18 Minnesota Golden Gophers are breaking into their lineup for the 2026-27 season. For the first three quarters of Monday’s season opener against Harvard, it definitely looked like a team that had not spent a ton of time playing together. But the Gophers took over and put together a complete final quarter to extend a two point lead after three quarters into a 20 point 82-62 win to open the season 1-0. Minnesota picked up three new players in the transfer portal and had a pair of impact freshmen that were all supposed to make an impact this season, and from game one we saw just that. All three transfers and both impact freshman played at least 14 minutes in the win over the Crimson led by Natalie Kussow’s 32 minutes. Kussow was in the Gophers starting lineup filling the void left by the injury to Tori McKinney and was joined by the expected pair of Mara Braun and Grace Grocholski along with a pair of transfers in Leah Harmon and Tayla Thomas. While Penn State center transfer Gracie Merkle did not start, she made the most of her 18 minutes off the bench leading the Gophers with 22 points. Minnesota and Harvard were locked in a back and forth battle for the first three quarters. Minnesota’s largest lead in the opening ten minutes was just four points as the Crimson kept close, and Minnesota struggled to shoot the long ball. In fact Minnesota did not make a three pointer until Grace Grocholski hit one with 4:06 left in the second quarter to put the Gophers up 28-25. A pair of Merkle layups gave the Gophers their largest lead of the game at that point of eight points, and a Harvard free throw would cut the lead to seven at halftime with Minnesota leading 37-30. Harvard came out the aggressors right away in the third quarter. A quick 7-0 aided by five Minnesota turnovers tied the game. It would take a Grocholski three with six seconds left in the third to put Minnesota back on top 54-52 headed into the final ten minutes. There the Gophers finally played up to their capabilities. They clamped down on defense and started taking the ball to the basket and getting open looks. Minnesota opened the quarter on a 21-4 run and never looked back. item.title: MLB Mariners hire 36-year-old Kanzler as new manager
item.description: Jason Kanzler has been named the new manager of Major League Baseball's Seattle Mariners (Michael Reaves) Jason Kanzler, player development director for the Chicago Cubs over the past three seasons, has been hired as manager of the Seattle Mariners, the Major League Baseball club announced Tuesday. Kanzler, in his first managerial post, becomes the 22nd manager in Mariners history and at age 36 is the second-youngest manager in MLB after Washington's 34-year-old Blake Butera. "Our goal in this process was finding a manager with the ability to challenge all of us to improve," Mariners president of baseball operations Jerry Dipoto said. "Jason has the mindset, expertise, communication skills, and intensity to help create a championship standard here in Seattle." Kanzler replaced Dan Wilson, who was dropped at the end of this year's campaign after just over two seasons with the Mariners in which he went 187-171. Seattle won the American League West division last year with a record of 90-72, but slid to 76-86 this year, settling for third in the division. "I'm thrilled to join the Mariners organization and I'm looking forward to hitting the ground running," Kanzler said. "This team has an immense amount of talent in all facets of the game and my coaching staff and I are excited to access and unlock this team's full potential." Kanzler served as an assistant coach for the Houston Astros in 2022 when they won the World Series and in 2023 before joining the Cubs. js/amz

For all of this team’s defensive woes throughout the season, it boasts the third-best defense in conference play while Pereira is top five in save percentage. Against Ohio State, Pereira made a number of incredible saves to keep NU alive in its push for an equalizer. item.title: Tyreek Hill’s Return To Chiefs Looks Dead After New Report
item.description: Rich Storry-Imagn Images Forget the dream of seeing Tyreek Hill in red and gold again. The path for him to play for the Kansas City Chiefs this season has effectively vanished. A recent civil jury verdict found Hill liable for two counts related to domestic violence, which complicates any potential move. On top of that, he is still rehabbing from multiple torn knee ligaments, a fact confirmed by RotoBaller. The timing is brutal. The calendar has flipped to November, which is long past the October return goal his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, had previously set. The Injury and Legal Double Whammy A nasty injury cut short Hill’s 2025 season. Now, at 31 years old, he has not signed with any NFL team. RotoBaller notes that fantasy managers should look elsewhere for help because of these issues. The legal trouble adds a massive layer of risk that no franchise wants to handle. Heavy.com reported that the jury verdict came down in a confusing civil case. The combination of a torn knee and a court finding of liability creates a wall that is nearly impossible to climb over. Chiefs Already Have Their Answers Even if Hill were healthy and cleared legally, the Chiefs do not need him. They already have young talent sitting on the roster who are not playing to their potential. ESPN’s Dan Graziano wrote a blunt assessment of the situation. “I know we do this all the time with the Chiefs, but they have guys. They just aren’t playing to their potential. Rashee Rice was a second-round pick. Xavier Worthy was a first-round pick! Remember how mad everybody got at the Bills for letting the Chiefs move up to take him? Guys like that are supposed to be the solutions.” Graziano points out that the team has high draft picks who should be the fix. Heavy.com notes that the Chiefs prefer using these existing players over signing a free agent. The logic is sound. Why bring in a 31-year-old with a bad knee and legal baggage when you have first-round picks waiting to step up? The front office knows this. They are looking at the trade deadline, but they are not looking at Hill. A Cold Reality for Fans The idea that Hill returns to Arrowhead is a story fans want to tell themselves, but the facts do not support it. He is not on a roster, he is injured, and he is facing serious legal scrutiny. The Chiefs have a game against the New York Jets on Sunday, Nov. 8. They will face that challenge with their current squad. The days of waiting for the former Miami Dolphins star to come home are over.

item.title: The transplanted Scot doing famous father proud in New Zealand
item.description: Clark Laidlaw has been head coach at Super Rugby champions Hurricanes for three seasons [Getty Images] A few weeks back, four Scots shot the breeze in New Zealand, a meeting of rugby intellects transplanted from Edinburgh, Inverness, Yetholm and Jedburgh - all of them doing great things in their adopted land. Mike Blair was one of them. On Saturday, in what promises to be a surreal day for him, the former Scotland captain will return to Murrayfield as attack coach for the All Blacks. Euan Mackintosh was another. Mackintosh is the All Blacks' skills acquisition coach. The third man was Adam Hay, who is New Zealand's performance scientist. The fourth was Clark Laidlaw, son of the great Roy, cousin of Greig and Super Rugby champion coach in 2026. "We were getting a bit of stick at lunch, the four of us talking Scottish," says Laidlaw, whose Hurricanes team not only won Super Rugby in late June, they dominated it. Finishing top of the table when the regular season ended, they won their first knockout game 66-12 against the Brumbies, then beat the Blues 57-21 in the semi-final before dismantling the Chiefs 60-5 in the final. It was Laidlaw's third season in charge. He's far more celebrated in New Zealand than he is at home. He's been there for 18 years, on and off, and he spoke about his life and times on the BBC's Scotland Rugby Podcast , how he went from a school-leaver at 16 to a New Zealand sevens coach - Commonwealth Games gold, World Cup Sevens gold, Olympics silver in Tokyo - to winning the ultimate club prize in southern hemisphere rugby in the summer. Laidlaw is a New Zealand passport holder now, but he'll be on Scotland's side on Saturday. "You're gonna see New Zealand's strongest possible team, but there's no reason why Scotland can't win," he reckons. "It's been a bounce of the ball here and there [in recent games]. item.title: Panthers Must Fix Left Tackle And Center Now
item.description: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images The Carolina Panthers offensive line is a mess, and the team cannot keep pretending it will fix itself. After a 27-19 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Thursday, the unit has become the main reason the offense stalls. Head coach Dave Canales acknowledged the possibility of changes in the offensive trenches. Swap the Starters at Center and Left Tackle First, the Panthers must bench veteran Luke Fortner at center. He has been a major disappointment for the team this year. Pro Football Focus reports Fortner has an overall grade of 53.3, placing him 30th among 35 qualifying centers. That is not good enough for a player who should be leading the line. Rookie Matt Hecht might not be perfect, but he cannot be worse than the current production. Hecht allowed just seven pressures in his final college season and zero sacks over 850 pass-blocking opportunities. The team should give the rookie a real shot to see if he can handle the job better than Fortner. Rasheed Walker was a bargain signing, but he has turned into the worst starter on the entire line. He keeps getting beat in pass protection and commits too many penalties. His PFF grade sits at 56.8, ranking 61st out of 71 qualifying offensive tackles across the league. Xavier Freeling, the replacement for 2026 first-round pick Ikem Ekwonu, is on the roster. Freeling spent practically his entire college career on the blindside at Georgia. For the remainder of the season, Freeling is slated to start at left tackle and Walker will move to the bench, per reports. This move alone could stop the constant pressure on the quarterback. Find a Real Tackle Before the Deadline Shuffling the bench players creates a hole on the right side. The logical name to fill that spot is Stone Forsythe, but he is not a great option. He is at best a below-average backup and cannot be counted on to start. With the NFL trade deadline approaching in one week, the Panthers must utilize it. They should look at Houston’s Braden Smith or Miami’s Austin Jackson. These players are available and would be a massive upgrade over what the team has now. The Panthers do not need to aim too high given their situation, but they must find someone who can actually protect the blindside. Canales said the changes come from the staff and their expectations for the players. “The urgency really just comes from myself, our staff, our expectations for our players, across the board,” Canales explained. The team is 3-4 and still leads the NFC South, but the record is misleading. The defense is struggling with injuries, and the offense cannot help them if the line keeps collapsing. Canales added that he wants his staff to feel confident in him. “We have a staff that’s committed to doing things the right way, and I want them to feel that confidence in me,” Canales added. item.title: Arsenal star wants to leave in January with European giants interested
item.description: Arsenal star wants to leave in January with European giants interested Martin Zubimendi Ready for Arsenal Exit as January Transfer Interest Builds Across Europe Martin Zubimendi appears to be moving towards an early Arsenal departure, with the midfielder now prepared to explore a January transfer after a difficult spell in north London. According to TeamTalk , the 27-year-old has reached an “exit decision” and several major clubs across Europe have been made aware of his situation. Zubimendi joined Arsenal in a £60million deal in 2025 amid strong competition and significant expectation. He arrived as a player expected to anchor Mikel Arteta’s midfield for years to come. Instead, his role has diminished sharply, and the latest information suggests the Spain international now sees a move as the best route to revive his career. January transfer picture becoming clearer The report states that “Martin Zubimendi is ready to leave Arsenal in January in a bid to get his career back on track” and that “seven of the continent’s biggest clubs” have now been informed. There is strong interest from Spain, where Real Madrid, Barcelona and Atletico Madrid are all said to be attentive to the opportunity. Germany is also a live market. Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund have reportedly been made aware of his availability, while there has been contact in England too. Chelsea have been spoken to, and Liverpool have also been informed, although their current thinking is described as less advanced. That point matters. Liverpool’s earlier admiration belonged to a different period and a different structure, and there is no suggestion at present that they are pushing aggressively to bring him in. The broader theme here is that Arsenal are facing a serious possibility of movement, and rival clubs know it. Photo IMAGO Zubimendi Arsenal struggle leaves club with decision The most striking detail in the report is how far Zubimendi’s standing has fallen. He was signed to be a first-choice option, yet he is “yet to start a Premier League game this season”. For a player of his pedigree, and for a fee of £60million, that is a major development. Competition in midfield has intensified. The arrival of Bruno Guimaraes has altered the landscape further, while “the decision to promote Myles Lewis-Skelly ahead of him last season” underlined the shift long before this campaign gathered pace. Arsenal are understood to be aware of the player’s feelings and the possibility that he will seek a move once the window reopens. There is also acknowledgement that any deal will need careful handling. A loan has been mentioned as one possible route, though the financial structure would need to make sense for all parties. Arsenal are not dealing with a fringe academy product here, they are trying to manage the future of a recent £60million signing whose value and reputation still carry weight across Europe. item.title: Dean Wade’s $38M Sixers Deal Echoes The Controversial PJ Tucker Era
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Philadelphia 76ers paid Dean Wade $38.7 million for a role that looks a lot like the one P.J. Tucker played here. The front office signed Wade to a four-year deal, yet his early minutes show zero points in a recent game against the New York Knicks. This lack of scoring aggression feels familiar to fans who watched Tucker struggle to find the net during his only full season in Philadelphia. Wade has played just five games so far, averaging 3.6 points and 3.0 rebounds while attempting only 2.0 shots from deep per game. According to The Sixer Sense , his tenure with the team reflects the same situation the Sixers faced with PJ Tucker, who shot 1.9 threes per game and scored 3.5 points. The numbers are strikingly similar for two players brought in to space the floor and defend the perimeter. Zero Shots in 27 Minutes The silence on offense is the loudest part of this story. In the game versus the Knicks, Wade found numerous open opportunities but went without a single field goal attempt over 27 minutes. Against the Pistons, he took just five shots in 30 minutes, a meager output for someone holding a max-level contract. Although he notched 10 assists against the Pistons, surpassing his prior career high, the roster requires more than passing when the clock runs low. LeBron James has praised Wade’s impact, stating last week that “Dean is a perfect player for every team, and he’s going to make winning plays.” Tyrese Maxey echoed this sentiment, telling reporters, “It felt like he was everywhere, right?” when discussing Wade’s defensive presence. The praise is real, but the contract requires more than just good defense and high basketball IQ. A Historic Shooting Slump The stats from Yahoo Sports paint a grim picture for a shooter. Wade shoots 30 percent from three on minimal volume, while his average stands at 4.5 field goal attempts per 100 possessions. This mark stands as the lowest among all qualified players in the league. The Sixers urged him to increase his shooting during training camp, but the results have not followed the instruction. He is currently tallying 3.0 rebounds and 3.6 points per game, playing close to 28 minutes each night. The front office pursued him for his defensive versatility and connective passing, which he has shown. Yet, a $38 million player producing two scoreless games in his first five contests is difficult to justify for a championship contender. The Sixers need Wade to find his shot soon, or this contract will look like a mistake before the season even hits its midpoint.

With big man Moustapha Thiam missing the season opener against Oakland with an illness, Boynton could’ve inserted freshman Quinn Costello or veteran Jalen Reed at the power forward spot. item.title: Simms Says Cowboys Growing Impatient With Dak Prescott Amid $131 Million Risk
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Former NFL quarterback Chris Simms believes the Dallas Cowboys are running out of patience with Dak Prescott. After a tough loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, Simms told listeners on his podcast that the team might be ready to move on. He noted that the franchise could be “at the end of their rope” with the veteran player if things do not improve quickly. The pressure is real, but the price to leave is even higher. Dallas signed Prescott to a massive four-year, $240 million extension in September 2024. That deal keeps him under contract through the 2028 season and includes $231 million in total guarantees. The team faces a nightmare scenario if they try to cut him now, as reported by Yahoo Sports . The Cost of Moving On Money is the main reason the Cowboys might keep Prescott despite the chatter. Dallas would face approximately $131 million in dead money if the player is cut prior to June 1, per reports. Even waiting until after June 1 does not solve the problem, as the team would still owe about $76 million. A trade offers slightly better relief but still carries a heavy cost of $86 million before the June deadline. These numbers mean the front office cannot just wave a wand and start over. The void years on Prescott’s deal, which run from 2029 through 2032, push the financial pain into the future. Sports Illustrated reported that the dead money hits would linger through 2030 because of these specific contract terms. Jerry Jones knows that paying for a player who does not start is bad business, but paying double for a new one is worse. Performance Under the Microscope Simms argues that Prescott simply does not match up with the best in the league. He stated on “PFT Live” that “Dak is not one of the top quarterbacks in football. The campaign was inspired by men’s basketball head coach Steve Pikiell and his wife, Kate, following Pikiell’s cancer diagnosis in September. Following surgery, the longtime Rutgers head coach expressed gratitude for the medical teams supporting him and his family as he continues treatment. Pikiell has also spoken about how his experience has changed his perspective on the people around him, particularly Rutgers fans who are dealing with cancer themselves. item.title: LeBron’s Wine Sip Proves The 76ers Are Finally Having Fun
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images During Monday night’s contest versus the Chicago Bulls, LeBron James sampled some red wine belonging to a fan. The Philadelphia 76ers won that matchup 126 to 107. James finished with 15 points, 7 rebounds, and 9 assists while the team moved to a 7-1 record on the season. The star player is no longer just grinding through the long season; he is enjoying the ride again. The moment happened in the third quarter when James chased a loose ball and crashed into fan Troy Clemons. Clemons was holding a cup of red wine, which is James’ favorite drink. James spilled some of the wine on himself and decided to taste it right there on the floor. He later told reporters, “I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm, how good it was. It was all right,” per ESPN . This wasn’t a planned stunt or a media event. It was a spontaneous reaction to a messy play. Sports often feel like a serious job for players, but this incident shows James treating the game like a party. He danced after an and-one layup that made guard Tyrese Maxey laugh. He also danced with Maxey later when the point guard scored his own and-one basket. These are the small moments that keep a player fresh. James explained the need for this joy clearly. He said, “Listen, it’s a long marathon. If you don’t find ways to have fun throughout it, even though you’re working, even though you’re locked in, then it could wear on you,” according to ESPN. Clemons, the fan who lost his wine, did not mind the exchange at all. He told ESPN, “I’m just glad for him to be here.” He even added, “I’m not worried about the wine getting on me.” The fan threw the cup away and got a fresh drink. He now has a story that will last a lifetime. The 76ers are 7-1, and the atmosphere in the arena feels lighter. This is what a winning team looks like when the players are actually happy. A Pattern of Fun in Philadelphia James has a history of playful moments involving alcohol during games. After missing a shot in 2017, he seized a beer bottle from a vendor, feigned drinking from it, then returned the bottle. That was a different time, but the spirit remains the same. On Monday, the interaction was more direct and personal. ESPN’s Kris Rhim posted a video of the event on X, captioning it, “Here’s vid of LeBron taking a sip of a drink from a fan just now during tonight’s game.” The video went viral because it felt real and unscripted. The 76ers face the Detroit Pistons on Wednesday. The Pistons are the only team to beat Philadelphia this season. The team needs to keep this fun energy if they want to stay on top. item.title: Patrick Kane Injury Sides Blackhawks, Missing Next Games
item.description: David Banks-Imagn Images The return of a legend hit a sudden snag on Monday night. Patrick Kane left the ice during the second period against Colorado and never came back. The Chicago Blackhawks confirmed he will sit out the next couple of games due to an upper-body injury. This loss comes right after a 5-2 defeat to the Avalanche, a result that already stung the home crowd. Head coach Jeff Blashill spoke clearly about the situation after the game. According to his statement, an upper-body injury has sidelined Kane for a minimum of two upcoming matches. The exact cause of the hurt remains unclear to the public. Before retreating to the locker room, Kane appeared to struggle physically, suggesting an underlying issue. His absence creates a gap in the lineup. A Heavy Loss for the Lineup The numbers show just how vital Kane is to this squad right now. At 37 years old, he has recorded one goal and eight assists for nine points in 14 games this season. Daily Faceoff reports he now shares the team’s top scoring spot with center Connor Bedard. The team will be without the player who shares the top spot with the franchise’s young star, a playmaker who creates scoring chances. Blashill noted the team must adjust without their veteran leader. The exact timeline for his return depends on how his body heals over the next few days. Fans saw him struggle near the end of the second period before the medical staff stepped in. The team released a brief statement confirming he will not return to the game on Monday, Nov. 2. This uncertainty hangs over the locker room as they prepare for their next opponent. History on the Line Kane’s journey back to Chicago was meant to be a celebration of his past glory. He signed a two-year, $16 million contract as an unrestricted free agent this past offseason. Prior to this, he played the preceding three seasons alongside the Detroit Red Wings. His legacy in Chicago is untouchable, having played his first 15-plus NHL seasons there. He won three Stanley Cups and earned the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP in 2013. His Hart Trophy win in 2016 proved he was the best player in the league during the regular season. He now sits second only to Stan Mikita on the Blackhawks’ historical scoring chart. Being named one of the NHL’s 100 Greatest Players in 2017 shows his standing in the sport. In 67 contests during the previous season, Kane recorded 16 goals and 41 assists totaling 57 points. Those stats prove he can still produce at a high level despite his age. Now, the team faces a test without its most experienced scorer. RotoWire reports that Ben Pope of the Chicago Sun-Times confirmed the injury details as well.

item.title: Hawks Win Looks Good But Hides Real Problems Against Six Pacers
item.description: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Atlanta needed a miracle just to beat a Pacers team that had no legs left. The Hawks escaped with a 108-104 win on Monday night in Indianapolis, but the final score tells a lie about how close this game actually was. Nickeil Alexander-Walker poured in 34 points and tied his career high with nine three-pointers, per Peachtree Hoops. Yet the team still let a squad with only six healthy players cut a 15-point lead down to two points in the final minutes. This was not a dominant performance. It was a lucky escape. A Salary Gap That Should Not Matter The story of this game was not the Hawks; it was the massive payroll the Pacers left on the bench. According to reports, the sidelined players totaled roughly $193 million in salary, whereas active court players earned approximately $15 million. Tyrese Haliburton, Pascal Siakam, and T.J. McConnell were all out, leaving Indiana with just six available bodies. Even with that huge gap, the Hawks struggled to put the game away. They shot just 28% from the field in the third quarter and endured a nearly four-minute field goal drought in the fourth. You do not get that kind of scare against a full-strength team. The Cost of a Bad Clutch Finish Atlanta had leads of 14 and 15 points but let them slip away due to poor execution down the stretch. Onyeka Okongwu finally hit a hook shot with 10.2 seconds left to secure a four-point lead, but the Pacers still had one more stop to make. Quenton Jackson missed a potential game-tying three-pointer with 43.1 seconds remaining, saving the Hawks from total embarrassment. The Pacers played with zero rest, as all six players logged between 34 and 45 minutes. Pacers coach Rick Carlisle admitted after the game that “These guys all played too many minutes,” according to theScore . If the Pacers had just one more body, the Hawks might have lost this one. Can This Team Handle Real Pressure? Head coach Quin Snyder called it a “really good win,” but the stats show a team that is still fragile when things get tight. The Hawks scored only 26 points in the paint all night, relying almost entirely on outside shooting to survive. Nickeil Alexander-Walker hit 15 of his 3-point attempts, and the team made 15 threes in the first half alone, tying a franchise record. But once the shooting cooled, the offense stalled completely. The Hawks will face the Washington Wizards on Wednesday, and they need to fix their interior scoring before that game. A win against a six-man team does not prove anything about their ability to beat a real contender.

item.description: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images The Detroit Pistons didn’t just beat the Hornets; they crushed them by 33 points in a 124-91 rout. When you add in their 29.6% shooting from deep, the offense looks stuck. Brandon Miller tried to keep things close with 17 points, but it wasn’t enough to stop the bleeding. The Pistons forced 27 turnovers and used those stops to build a massive lead that the Hornets could never touch. Duncan Robinson Is the Difference Maker In his first start of the season, he made six of his nine 3-point attempts and scored 24 points. His energy sparked a 27-2 run in the third quarter that effectively ended the game. Robinson explained the shift simply after the game. “We got stops,” Duncan Robinson commented on that key moment. “I think they were stuck at 75 for a while. When we get stops, the game becomes really easy for us.” The Pistons also got 11 points from Ron Holland II, who stayed in the game late and kept the pressure on. This depth is what separates a good team from a great one. Charlotte fans are used to seeing their team struggle, but this loss feels different. The Hornets led the league in 3-pointers made last season, yet they are now tied for 16th in makes this year. Naz Reid is averaging a career-high 15.5 points, but his shooting percentage has dropped to 39.5%. The team needs to find a way to score without relying solely on the outside shot. Detroit has shown they can punish teams that make mistakes, and the Hornets made plenty of them. The Pistons will host the Philadelphia 76ers on Wednesday, but the Hornets face the Brooklyn Nets on the road.

item.title: Chiefs Rookie Delane Faces Long Road Back From Shoulder Injury
item.description: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs are watching their rookie cornerback, Mansoor Delane, closely as he tries to get his shoulder strong enough to play. Head coach Andy Reid gave fans a mixed update after the team lost to the Denver Broncos on Sunday. While Delane has played well this season, his right shoulder keeps acting up and might be a problem for the rest of the year. The team needs him back, but safety comes first. Reid said on Monday that the rookie could return for the game against the New York Jets, yet he warned that the injury is not going away quickly. Delane missed the last game against Denver even though he was listed as questionable before the start. The issue started back in the offseason during organized team activities and has troubled him ever since. He aggravated the shoulder during a Week 1 win over the Broncos and sat out the rest of that game plus all of Week 2. He played in four straight games after returning, but the pain flared up again in practice last Wednesday. This forced the Chiefs to rule him out for Sunday’s matchup at Empower Field at Mile High. A Day-By-Day Battle for Strength The coaching staff will not rush Delane back until his body is ready. Reid explained that the team will check on him every single day to see how he feels. “It’s just a matter of it being strong enough to get out there,” Reid said. The coach added that there is a chance Delane can play in Week 9, but it depends entirely on how strong the shoulder gets. “There’s a chance that he’ll be able to get himself out there this week. Again, it’s just how strong it is. It’s going to be a day-to-day thing,” Reid told reporters. The first practice of the week on Wednesday will show if he can take the field. Delane has shown he is a key player when healthy. Yahoo Sports reports that in five games this season, he has posted 27 tackles, five passes defended, and one interception. item.title: ‘So fake’… NBA fans react to LeBron James saying he enjoyed being Russell Westbrook’s teammate
item.description: Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images LeBron James has paid tribute to former teammate Russell Westbrook – but fans are not buying it. Russell Westbrook announced his retirement from the NBA in the offseason, ending a long career that peaked by winning the MVP in the 2016-17 season. He became the first player to ever average a triple-double for an entire season. Westbrook’s jersey will be retired by the Oklahoma City Thunder, and his former LA Lakers teammate LeBron James has paid tribute to him, speaking to the Mind The Game podcast . James said: “I think one of the things about Russ that doesn’t get talked about is like the guy never wanted to take a night off. Wanted to play in every single game. Being a teammate of his for that year or two, I think it was a year and a half, maybe two years in LA. He never wanted to take a game off. “Never wanted to take a practice off. Great dude. You can never, it’s not going to be one person that played with him in the locker room and he like, man, he wasn’t a good teammate like, everyone raves about him, including myself. “Kudos to him and that jacket, that Hall of Fame jacket is next.” The Lakers traded for Westbrook in 2021, striking a deal with the Wizards in exchange for Kyle Kuzma, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Montrezl Harrell, and a 2021 first-round pick. The move was a spectacular failure, with ball-dominant Westbrook and James failing to gel on the court. The Lakers won only 33 games in 2021-22, having lost key depth including Alex Caruso, who was allowed to walk for financial reasons. Frank Vogel was fired and replaced by Darvin Ham, who relegated Westbrook into a bench role. The Lakers eventually traded Westbrook to the Jazz in February 2023. LeBron James slammed for Westbrook comments LeBron James’ tribute to Russell Westbrook has raised eyebrows, after their dysfunctional time on the Lakers together. One fan wrote on social media: “Bron knows deep down he hated playing with him.” A second fan hit out: “LeBron is so fake. He was begging the Lakers to get rid of Russell Westbrook.” Another added: “He just playing it up for the camera, we all know Russ was a locker room vampire.” A third fan noted: “There’s always such an obvious lack of enthusiasm when he talks about Russ.” And another comment added: “Says the dude who used him as a scapegoat.” James eventually moved on from the LA Lakers earlier this year, signing with the Philadelphia 76ers. The 41-year-old appears to be enjoying his basketball a lot more right now than during the Lakers-Westbrook era – which might just have been the least enjoyable from James’ career, at least looking from the outside. item.title: How Oregon State turned a raw athlete into a starting linebacker
item.description: CORVALLIS — Two years ago, Jarrel Comer was a freshman at Tallahassee Community College and had not played competitive football since middle school. Now he’s a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State . Comer played basketball at Eastside High School in Gainesville, Florida, but began college as a regular student. He looked for opportunities to play sports again and football became the opportunity at Citrus College in California. He boarded a plane for the first time to take a cross-country flight to play football for the first time in more than four years. “I was willing to take that chance to get to where I am today,” Comer said.
